text:
Marathon Petroleum stock rose slightly today, gaining 0.66%, as crude oil prices stabilized after falling sharply earlier in the week. U.S. oil dropped nearly 8% last week following diplomatic talks between Tehran and Washington at the U.N., which eased immediate concerns about supply disruption in the Middle East. With refineries running at 94% capacity and crude inventories relatively stable, the modest bounce today reflects a momentary pause in the downward pressure that weighed on energy stocks earlier in the week.

The broader backdrop remains volatile: while Iran has signaled willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear negotiations, Saudi Arabia is simultaneously ramping up crude exports despite attacks on its infrastructure from Iran-backed militants. This creates genuine uncertainty about whether oil prices will stabilize here or face renewed pressure if diplomatic talks progress—refinery stocks like Marathon tend to benefit from lower input costs (crude oil), so the 8% weekly oil drop has been a headwind despite today's small uptick.
